rect.title: This diagram is drawn from ply.yaml, the file describing this codebase's architecture and verification claims. Each box is a component; chips are functions with their declared checks; arrows are permitted calls (solid) and data flows (dashed); red bars are forbidden calls. A box's grey depth is how strongly it promises to be checked — white means something inside promises nothing, deeper grey means stronger checks promised, and the weakest function sets the whole box's shade. Nothing here is green: green is kept for evidence a run has actually earned, which this render never sees, so a picture full of promises should not look like a picture full of results. Hover anything for its meaning. completed evidence: verdict: fuzzed(64) statuses: none reused: no

g.title: ply.yaml — the document this picture is drawn from. Everything you see here was declared in it; nothing was inferred from code. What each box has actually been checked for is what `cargo ply verify` reports, not this drawing. ply: 1 — the format version every rule below is read under; a version this build does not speak is refused, never guessed at

What this document declares. "0 functions promise nothing" counts functions that end up with nothing checked -- whether nobody wrote any checks for them, or the document switched checking off for them on purpose. Running `cargo ply verify` is what turns promises into results, and its last run reported: 3 the promise held, 0 broken, 0 a tool could not settle either way, 0 out of date since that run.

component greendemo — maps to Rust module greendemo declares checks up to fuzzed — checked against many random inputs — the strongest verdict this could earn if every declared check ran and passed; a promise, never a result this box is this shade because `digit_count` is the weakest thing in it: it declares fuzzed — checked against many random inputs — nothing here is drawn stronger than its weakest part completed evidence: verdict: fuzzed(64) statuses: none reused: no

clamp bounded(2) — Kani symbolically checks supported inputs that satisfy requires against ensures; 2 is the maximum loop-unwind depth, not a numeric input limit; collection inputs may also be limited to length 2 fuzz(64) — tries 64 generated inputs that satisfy requires, then checks ensures input and post contract: Input (requires): lo <= hi Postcondition (ensures): |result|*result >= lo && *result <= hi the checks above are what will test the function against exactly this promise when `cargo ply verify` runs a run actually checked this and the promise held — this is a real result, not just a plan completed evidence: verdict: bounded(2) statuses: none reused: no engine: proptest seed: 571829bcfd61f2823c67250aae5d15ca8127d41b4990c8d88e387b2ff17ca93d cases: 64 source: src/lib.rs:3:0-8:1 warning W0503: most of the inputs generated for `clamp` were thrown away by its own `#[ply::requires]` precondition (69/133 draws rejected). proptest kept drawing until it had 64 accepted cases, so the count is honest -- but those cases all come from the narrow corner of the input space the precondition allows, which is weaker evidence than 64 on its own suggests. (W0503)

digit_count fuzz(64) — tries 64 generated inputs that satisfy requires, then checks ensures input and post contract: Postcondition (ensures): |result|*result <= text.len() the checks above are what will test the function against exactly this promise when `cargo ply verify` runs a run actually checked this and the promise held — this is a real result, not just a plan completed evidence: verdict: fuzzed(64) statuses: none reused: no engine: proptest seed: b9f47809fa4b23cad8db2e3c1d230f530ffd8655928847c40e5ef637d962166f cases: 64 source: src/lib.rs:10:0-14:1 info W0521: `digit_count` was checked using randomly generated text (up to 32 characters). By default, Ply never generates ASCII or Latin-1 control characters (raw bytes like a null byte or an escape code, `0x00`-`0x1F` and `0x7F`-`0x9F`) -- the kind of byte real user-facing text almost never contains, and the kind most likely to trip an unrelated assumption (a log line, a terminal, a CSV cell) rather than `digit_count`'s own logic, so including them would risk a false alarm rather than a real bug. Multi-byte Unicode text (accented letters, CJK characters, symbols) is NOT excluded -- Ply generates it deliberately, since a `String` a real caller holds can already contain it. If `digit_count` needs to handle control characters correctly, this run says nothing about that -- it was never asked to. (W0521, §5.4c)

total fuzz(64) — tries 64 generated inputs that satisfy requires, then checks ensures input and post contract: Postcondition (ensures): |result|*result >= a && *result >= b the checks above are what will test the function against exactly this promise when `cargo ply verify` runs a run actually checked this and the promise held — this is a real result, not just a plan completed evidence: verdict: fuzzed(64) statuses: none reused: no engine: proptest seed: bc68ec89be2ebc8953498e33f76c95fe0ed5488ccf4a48bfa5a4edfcab3dd6da cases: 64 source: src/lib.rs:16:0-18:59
